title: Exact short-horizon planning is not general adaptive consistency
statement: A positive-gain decoy can keep one-step greedy blind to a two-coordinate parity interaction; more generally any horizonB<d gives a symmetric d-way parity component zero value, even adaptively, and an exact short-horizon planner can ignore it forever. Paid forced exploration may restore a different consistency property but is not an optimal finite-cost guarantee. Separately, binary-symmetric and erasure selector channels share mean,prior variance,cost,learned variancea^2 and even a one-use whole fixed-budget profile, but adaptive mux continuation gains differ byu a(1-2a)>0 (at a1/4,u1/16,gains9/256 versus7/256). The continuation depends on E|M-1/2| absent from that profile. This rejects the scalar interface for arbitrary adaptive contexts, not the fixed-independent Phi theorem or every richer compact interface; it is not a claim that identical fully retained Beta hyperparameters hide distinct fixed-count channels.

requires: Horizon example: independent symmetric Beta parity parameters plus the stated positive-gain decoy and a horizon smaller than the interaction order.
Profile example: the explicit one-use binary-symmetric/erasure local channels and independent equal-mean mux branches with the supplied continuation experiments.
The generic channel comparison does not identify two distinct fully retained Beta-Bernoulli hyperparameter experiments.
